# Tarneeb-RL — Technical Blueprint v1.2

**Document version:** 1.2
**Supersedes:** v1.1 (which superseded v1.0)
**Rules version defined here:** `tarneeb-classic-v1`
**Observation spec version:** `obs_v2`
**Action spec version:** `act_v1`
**Event schema version:** `event_v1`
**Buffer / replay contract version:** `chunk_v2` (new in v1.2)
**Status:** specification only. No production code is generated by this document.

**What changed in v1.2, in one line each.** (1) The event-consumption convention is now mathematically defined so no event is consumed twice and the epoch-zero PPO ratio is provably 1. (2) The critic now has per-seat recurrent state. (3) League seating and gradient ownership are fully specified. (4) T-E2 no longer asserts a property a neural network cannot guarantee. (5) All parameter counts recomputed including LayerNorm and GRU biases. (6) Potential-based shaping now defines `Φ(terminal) = 0` and states its assumptions. (7) DQN/A2C/TRPO are reframed as a scope decision, not a refutation. (8) `defender_kaboot_bonus` is frozen. (9) The 98-case scoring table wording is corrected. (10) `K_MAX` is proved to be 14 and set to 16.

---

## Evidence labelling convention

| Tag | Meaning |
|---|---|
| **[Direct]** | Evidence about Tarneeb itself, or about a tool/library's documented behaviour. |
| **[Inferred]** | Evidence transferred from a different game or benchmark. The reasoning is stated; the result is *not* proven for Tarneeb. |
| **[Engineering judgement]** | My design opinion. No external evidence. Falsifiable by your own experiments. |
| **[Derived]** | A mathematical consequence of definitions in this document, checkable by hand or by the cited computation. |

Nothing in this document reports a completed experiment. Every performance number attached to *this* project is a **target** or a **prediction** and is written as such.

---

## 0. Scope note and literature position

At least one directly relevant peer-reviewed conference paper on Tarneeb RL exists:

> Leina Abouhagar and Emmanuel Okafor, "An Empirical Analysis of Deep Reinforcement Learning for Playing Tarneeb Game," *2025 IEEE Gaming, Entertainment, and Media Conference (GEM)*, 2025.
> DOI: [10.1109/GEM66882.2025.11155259](https://doi.org/10.1109/GEM66882.2025.11155259)
> IEEE Xplore document: [11155259](https://ieeexplore.ieee.org/document/11155259)

See §18.1 for the verified record, including an explicit list of what could and could not be verified.

Corrected position:

1. **[Direct]** Tarneeb RL research exists. It is small, recent, and single-agent-framed, but it exists and must be cited.
2. **[Direct]** That paper compares PPO, A2C, TRPO and DQN in a custom Gym-compatible Tarneeb environment and reports PPO best. This **supports** choosing PPO as this project's primary baseline.
3. **[Direct]** Its reported evaluation — 20 test game cycles against a deterministic opponent — is too small to establish PPO as optimal, and the accessible abstract reports no confidence intervals, seed counts, or self-play.
4. **[Inferred]** It says nothing about recurrent policies, centralized critics, partner-diversity training, or league self-play. Those remain hypotheses transferred from Bridge, Mahjong, DouDizhu and Hanabi, and must be tested by ablation.

The literature search was **not exhaustive**. Arabic-language theses and regional papers may exist. Every novelty claim in this document is hedged accordingly (§18).

## 1. Executive Recommendation

| # | Original hypothesis | v1.2 recommendation | Why |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | PettingZoo AEC as the training interface | **Custom engine + custom vectorized turn-based rollout collector.** PettingZoo AEC wrapper kept as a conformance artifact | **[Direct]** No maintained library combines masking + recurrence + centralized critic + league. SB3-contrib's `MaskablePPO` documents that recurrent policies are not supported. RLlib is mid-migration to its "new API stack" |
| 2 | Episode = full match to 31 | **Episode = one deal** for stages 1–9; full match only at stage 11 | **[Engineering judgement]**, supported by **[Inferred]** Suphx separating per-round outcome from the final multi-round reward via a learned global reward predictor |
| 3 | Pure RL from scratch | **Behaviour-clone the strong heuristic first, then RL** | **[Inferred]** Lockhart et al. bootstrapped bridge bidding by imitating a hand-coded human-compatible bot, then applying search and policy iteration |
| 4 | MAPPO as final | **Recurrent PPO + centralized critic (MAPPO-style), with IPPO as a mandatory ablation** | **[Inferred]** MAPPO's evidence is cooperative-only; IPPO matched joint-critic methods on SMAC. Direction genuinely unknown for a two-team competitive game |
| 5 | Not mentioned | **Partner-diversity / cross-play evaluation from day one** | **[Inferred]** Naive self-play produces private conventions that break with novel partners |
| 6 | Not mentioned | **Lock the rule variant in writing before writing code** | **Done.** §2 freezes `tarneeb-classic-v1` |
| 7 | Flat "current high bid" history features | **A single canonical ordered `PublicEvent` stream** | v1.0 could lose earlier bids and passes. §5 fixes this |
| 8 | **NEW in v1.2** — ambiguous event consumption between rollout and replay | **A single formal consumption convention (§10.1) with an exactness proof and an epoch-zero ratio test** | v1.1's replay loop fed the chunk-head events again after they were already folded into the stored hidden state, which would have made the epoch-zero ratio ≠ 1 and silently corrupted every PPO update |

### 1.1 The three algorithm decisions

1. **Simplest learning baseline — masked PPO, feedforward history encoder, one deal per episode, fixed trump, shared parameters, heuristic opponents.** **[Direct]** Supported by Abouhagar & Okafor (2025).
2. **Primary final algorithm — recurrent (GRU-over-events) PPO with a centralized full-information critic, shared actor parameters across all four seats, trained under a PFSP league.** **[Inferred]**; validated by ablations A1, A2, A3, A7.
3. **Advanced research extension — test-time belief search.** **[Inferred]** Bridge results show self-play RL plus a test-time search beat WBridge5 by 0.98 IMPs/deal over 10,000 deals, above a prior 0.85 IMPs state of the art.

### 1.2 MVP / Final / Optional

| Tier | Contents |
|---|---|
| **MVP** (weeks 1–7) | Engine + tests + 3 baseline agents + CLI human play + masked feedforward PPO with the padded event-history block + evidence of learning |
| **Final research system** (weeks 8–13) | Event-GRU policy + per-seat centralized critic + PFSP league + full ablation suite + deployment + written report |
| **Optional** | Test-time search, transformer event encoder, other-play suit symmetry, Egyptian bidding variant, larger human study |

## 2. Formal Tarneeb Specification — `tarneeb-classic-v1`

### 2.1 Sources consulted

| Source | Link | Contribution |
|---|---|---|
| Pagat (John McLeod), *Tarneeb* | https://www.pagat.com/auctionwhist/tarneeb.html | The most carefully sourced English description of the classic game, plus the regional variation list |
| Wikipedia, *Tarneeb* | https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tarneeb | Independent corroboration; target 41 with 31/61 noted regionally |
| Tarneeb.com / YallaPlay | https://www.tarneeb.com/rules | Deployed commercial implementation |
| Jawaker, *Tarneeb* | https://www.jawaker.com/en/rules/tarneeb | Largest Arabic card platform; trump suits enumerated; kaboot scoring |
| Jawaker, *Syrian Tarneeb 41* | https://jawaker.com/pt/rules/tarneeb_syrian41 | Regional target-score variation |
| Jawaker, *Tarneeb Masrawy (Egyptian)* | https://blog.jawaker.com/en/tarneeb-masrawy-rules-en | The Egyptian suit-bidding variant, excluded from v1 |
| gambiter, *Tarneeb* | https://gambiter.com/cards/Tarneeb.html | Set ends at 31; Lebanese one-bid form; mandatory trump lead regionally |
| catsatcards, *Tarneeb* | https://catsatcards.com/Games/Tarneeb.html | Dealer-may-equal; all-pass redeal |
| "King Tarneeb" app rules | https://apps.apple.com/us/app/id1409529888 | An implementation matching §2.2's scoring table (16 / 26 / −16), target 31 |
| Jawaker, *Tarneeb 400* | https://www.jawaker.com/en/rules/tarneeb400 | Listed **only** so it is never confused with Tarneeb; it is a different game |

**No source describing a distinctly *Jordanian* variant separate from the general Levantine game was found.** Jordan is consistently grouped with Lebanon, Syria and Palestine. `tarneeb-classic-v1` is the documented classic Levantine game. If your local table plays differently, that is a configuration change, not a spec error.

### 2.2 The frozen specification

| ID | Rule | Value |
|---|---|---|
| C01 | Players | 4, two fixed partnerships, partners opposite |
| C02 | Deck | 52 cards, A K Q J 10 9 8 7 6 5 4 3 2 (A high) |
| C03 | Hand size | 13 per player |
| C04 | Direction | Counter-clockwise for bidding and play |
| C05 | Dealer | Random first deal; thereafter passes to the right |
| C06 | First bidder | The player to the dealer's right |
| C07 | Bid range | Integers 7..13 |
| C08 | Bid ordering | Each new bid strictly greater than the current high bid |
| C09 | Passing | A pass removes the player from that auction permanently |
| C10 | All pass | Hand thrown in, redealt **by the same dealer** |
| C11 | Auction end | Exactly one active bidder remains and a bid exists; that player is the declarer |
| C12 | Trump selection | The declarer chooses one of the four suits |
| C13 | No-trump | **Not available.** See §2.3 |
| C14 | Opening lead | The declarer leads to the first trick |
| C15 | Lead constraint | None |
| C16 | Following suit | Must follow the led suit if able |
| C17 | Void | May play any card, trump or otherwise |
| C18 | Trick winner | Highest trump; if no trump, highest card of the led suit |
| C19 | Next lead | The trick winner leads |
| C20 | Contract made | Bidding team scores its trick count; defenders score 0 |
| C21 | Contract failed | Bidding team scores −(bid); defenders score their tricks |
| C22 | Kaboot after a bid < 13 | All 13 tricks scores 16 (13 + 3) |
| C23 | Bid of 13 made | 26 to the bidding team |
| C24 | Bid of 13 failed | −16 to the bidding team; defenders score **twice** their tricks |
| **C26** | **Defender kaboot** (**frozen in v1.2**) | **A defending team that takes all 13 tricks scores 16.** `defender_kaboot_bonus = True`, `defender_kaboot_score = 16` |
| C25 | Match end | First team to reach 31 or more points wins |

**On C26 — an explicit project rule, no longer an open question.** Jawaker states that a team winning all 13 tricks without having bid them adds 16 points, and Pagat's kaboot wording is team-neutral; the "King Tarneeb" implementation phrases the 16-point award as applying to the bidding side only. Both readings are attested. **This project selects the 16-point defender form** because it is directly documented and because it makes the kaboot rule symmetric between the two teams, which removes a special case from the scoring function. Other tables may score 13; that is preserved as the separately versioned configuration `defender_kaboot_13`, which would be released as `tarneeb-classic-v1-alt13` with its own rules fingerprint. **This is not a blocker and is removed from §22.**

### 2.3 The no-trump decision

**Ruling: no-trump is NOT part of `tarneeb-classic-v1`.** `allow_no_trump = False`.

| Source | Position |
|---|---|
| Wikipedia | The declarer announces a *tarneeb (trump) suit*. No-trump never mentioned |
| Jawaker (classic) | Trump chosen from four enumerated suits |
| Jawaker (Syrian 41) | Same |
| Tarneeb.com / YallaPlay | Highest bidder picks the trump **suit** |
| "King Tarneeb" | Final bidder announces the trump **suit** |
| catsatcards | Declarer states the trump **suit** |
| **Pagat** | **The one classic source that mentions it**, as an option |
| Jawaker (Egyptian) | No-trump is central *there*, ranking above spades |

**Action-space consequence.** The action space stays at **65**. Action ID 64 (`TRUMP_NT`) is **reserved and permanently masked**. Rationale: checkpoint portability across the flag (a 64-wide head would break `load_state_dict`); the masked logit receives `torch.finfo(dtype).min` so its probability is exactly 0 and it contributes nothing to the masked entropy; the cost is 257 unused parameters out of ~957k (0.027%). Test I13 asserts action 64 is illegal in every reachable state, never sampled across 1,000,000 masked samples, and receives exactly zero gradient.

### 2.5 Formal state machine

Seats `P = {0,1,2,3}` counter-clockwise. Teams `T0 = {0,2}`, `T1 = {1,3}`. Dealer `d`. First bidder `(d+1) mod 4`.

| Phase | Actor | Actions | Legality | Transition | Ends when | Emits events |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **DEAL** (chance) | — | shuffle + deal | — | `hands[p] ← 13`; `high_bid←∅`; `active←{0..3}`; `turn←(d+1)%4`; `event_seq←0` | immediately | none |
| **BID** | `turn ∈ active` | `PASS`, `BID(v)`, `v∈7..13` | `BID(v)` iff `v > high_bid` (or `high_bid=∅`); `PASS` always | `PASS`: `active ← active\{turn}`. `BID(v)`: `high_bid←v`, `high_bidder←turn`. `turn ←` next active CCW | `\|active\|=1 ∧ high_bid≠∅` → DECLARE; `\|active\|=0` → REDEAL | `BID` or `PASS` |
| **DECLARE** | `declarer` | `TRUMP(s)`, `s∈{♣,♦,♥,♠}` | always (ID 64 masked) | `trump←s`; `leader←declarer`; `trick←[]`; `trick_no←0` | after one action | `TRUMP_SELECTED` |
| **PLAY** | `turn` | `CARD(c)` | `c ∈ hand` ∧ (follows led suit ∨ void in led suit) | remove `c`; append; `turn←next CCW`. On the 4th card: resolve, `tricks_won[winner_team]+=1`, `leader←winner`, `trick_no+=1`, `trick←[]` | `trick_no = 13` → SCORE | `CARD_PLAYED`; plus `TRICK_COMPLETED` on the 4th card |
| **SCORE** | — | — | — | apply §2.6 | immediately | `DEAL_COMPLETED` |
| **MATCH** | — | — | — | if `max(match_score) ≥ target` → TERMINAL, else `d←(d+1)%4`, → DEAL | — | none |

### 2.6 Scoring function

Let `b` = winning bid, `B` = bidding team, `D` = defending team, `t_B` = tricks won by `B`, `t_D = 13 − t_B`.

```
score_deal(b, t_B, rules) -> (ΔS_B, ΔS_D)

  if b == 13:
      if t_B == 13:  return (+26, 0)                              # C23
      else:          return (-16, rules.bid13_failed_defender_multiplier * t_D)   # C24
  # b < 13
  if t_B == 13:      return (+16, 0)                              # C22 bidder kaboot
  if t_B >= b:       return (+t_B, 0)                             # C20
  if t_D == 13:      return (-b, 16)                              # C26 defender kaboot (frozen)
  return (-b, t_D)                                                # C21
```

**Reward bounds. [Derived]** With `Δ = ΔS_B − ΔS_D` from the bidding team's view:

- Maximum: `+26` (bid 13, made).
- Minimum: `−16 − 2·13 = −42` (bid 13, failed, defenders take all 13).
- Therefore `Δ ∈ [−42, +26]` for the bidding team, `[−26, +42]` for defenders, so `|Δ| ≤ 42` for every seat.

The C26 freeze does not change these bounds: the defender-kaboot branch has `b ≤ 12`, giving `Δ = −b − 16 ≥ −28 > −42`.

### 2.7 Game classification

| Level | Formalism | Justification |
|---|---|---|
| Whole game | **Two-team zero-sum POSG** | Four agents, private observations, stochastic deal, opposing team objectives. Per-deal points are not constant-sum; the match outcome is binary between two teams |
| One team, opponents frozen | **Dec-POMDP** | Two agents share a payoff and cannot communicate outside the game's own channel. **[Inferred]** the Hanabi setting |
| One agent, all others frozen | **POMDP** | The basis of independent learning (IPPO) |

Never call Tarneeb a Dec-POMDP unqualified. It is one only conditional on frozen opponents, and that conditionality is why league training is required.

### 2.8 State-space complexity

| Quantity | Value | Method |
|---|---|---|
| Distinct deals | 53,644,737,765,488,792,839,237,440,000 ≈ 5.36×10²⁸ | `52!/(13!)⁴`, computed |
| Distinct hands for one player | 635,013,559,600 | `C(52,13)`, computed |
| **Distinct auction action-sequences** | **1,823** | exhaustive enumeration of C06–C11 |
| Auction internal decision nodes | 2,528 | same enumeration |
| Auctions × trump choice | **7,292** | `1823 × 4` |
| Maximum auction length | **10 actions** | 7 strictly increasing bids + 3 passes; verified by enumeration |
| Maximum public events per deal | **77** | `10 + 1 TRUMP_SELECTED + 52 CARD_PLAYED + 13 TRICK_COMPLETED + 1 DEAL_COMPLETED` |

**Play-phase estimate — [Engineering judgement].** With 52 plies and an average legal branching factor of 4–5, play sequences per deal are roughly `4^52 ≈ 2×10^31` to `5^52 ≈ 2×10^36`. Total tree size ≈ `10^63`–`10^68`. **Measure the true branching factor in week 3 and replace this estimate.**

**Why tabular methods are impossible.** A table over just the 6.35×10¹¹ hands, ignoring history, at 4 bytes each needs 2.5 TB. Function approximation is mandatory.

### 3.2 Selection decisions

**Corrected wording in v1.2.** The column below says *why this project does not implement an algorithm*, which is a scope decision under a fixed student budget. It is **not** a claim that the algorithm is universally inferior for Tarneeb. The only directly relevant Tarneeb comparison reports 20 test-game cycles against a single deterministic opponent, which is far too little evidence to rank algorithms definitively.

| Algorithm | Sample eff. | Stability | Guarantee | Compute | Impl. difficulty | Framework support | Selection decision |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Tabular Q | n/a | n/a | yes (tiny MDPs) | trivial | trivial | any | **Not selected.** Ruled out on complexity grounds alone: 10⁶³ states. This one *is* a hard exclusion |
| DQN | Med | Low-Med | none | Low | Low | SB3 | **Not selected as a primary baseline.** The only directly relevant Tarneeb comparison reported PPO highest and DQN lowest of four; that is a single small study, not a refutation. Combined with a limited budget better spent on recurrence, critic centralization and league training, DQN is out of scope for v1. **[Inferred]** DouZero was designed partly to avoid DQN's overestimation bias, which is suggestive for card games but not proof for Tarneeb |
| Double/Dueling DQN | Med | Med | none | Low | Low-Med | SB3 / contrib | **Not selected.** Same scope reasoning. These fix overestimation but do not address partial observability or the mask + memory combination this project needs |
| DRQN | Low | Low | none | Med | Med | none turnkey | **Not selected.** Recurrent replay is fragile and would consume the week-8 budget that recurrent PPO needs |
| A2C | Low | Low | none | Low | Low | SB3 | **Not selected as a primary baseline.** Reported below PPO in the one Tarneeb study; a scope decision, not evidence of universal inferiority |
| TRPO | Med | High | approx. monotonic improvement | Med | High | sb3-contrib | **Not selected as a primary baseline.** Reported below PPO in the one Tarneeb study, and the conjugate-gradient step is substantially more code than clipping. Scope decision |
| **PPO (masked, FF)** | Med | **High** | none | Low | Low-Med | sb3-contrib `MaskablePPO` | **✅ BASELINE.** **[Direct]** Highest of four in the Tarneeb comparison; **[Inferred]** the standard on-policy choice under non-stationarity |
| IPPO | Med | High | none | Med | Med | custom | **✅ MANDATORY ABLATION (A2)** |
| Recurrent PPO | Med | Med-High | none | Med | Med-High | sb3-contrib `RecurrentPPO` — **not together with masking** | Stepping stone |
| MAPPO | Med | High | none | Med | Med-High | custom | Component of final |
| **Recurrent MAPPO** | Med | Med-High | none | Med-High | High | **custom only** | **✅ PRIMARY** |
| NFSP | Low | Med | 2-player zero-sum only | High | High | OpenSpiel | **Not selected.** Its guarantees do not extend to 4-player team games. This is a structural mismatch, not merely scope |
| CFR | n/a | n/a | 2p zero-sum, tabular | impossible | Med | OpenSpiel | **Not selected.** Structural: cannot enumerate 10⁶³ information sets |
| Deep CFR | Low | Med | approx., 2p zero-sum | very high | very high | OpenSpiel | **Not selected.** Structural mismatch plus compute far beyond budget |
| IS-MCTS | n/a | High | none | high per move | Med | OpenSpiel | **✅ EXTENSION** |
| AlphaZero-style | High | High | none | very high | very high | OpenSpiel | **Not selected.** Structural: assumes perfect information |
| **Imitation → RL** | **High** | High | none | Low | Low-Med | custom | **✅ ADOPT as initialiser** |

Note the distinction the table now draws: *structural* exclusions (tabular Q, CFR family, NFSP, AlphaZero) are principled, while *scope* exclusions (DQN, Double/Dueling DQN, DRQN, A2C, TRPO) are budget decisions that a future project could revisit with a proper evaluation.

### 3.3 Why PPO, stated correctly

**[Direct]** Abouhagar & Okafor (2025) trained PPO, A2C, TRPO and DQN in a custom Gym-compatible Tarneeb environment, evaluated over 20 test game cycles against a deterministic opponent; all four exceeded a 55% win rate and PPO was highest at 65%.

- ✅ Licenses **PPO as the starting baseline** for Tarneeb specifically rather than by analogy.
- ✅ Justifies **spending this project's limited budget elsewhere** than re-running an algorithm bake-off.
- ❌ Does **not** establish PPO as optimal, and does **not** refute the alternatives.
- ❌ Says nothing about recurrence, centralized critics, league self-play or partner diversity — the parts of this project that could contribute.

**Report wording to reuse verbatim:** *DQN, A2C and TRPO are not selected as primary implementation baselines because the only directly relevant Tarneeb comparison reported PPO highest, while this project's limited budget is better spent testing recurrence, critic centralization and league training. This is a scope decision, not evidence that the alternatives are universally inferior.*

## 4. Simulator Design

### 4.1 Framework decision

| Option | Verdict | Reason |
|---|---|---|
| **Pure Python custom core** | **✅ PRIMARY** | The only way to get masking + event stream + per-seat critic + league in one system |
| Gymnasium | `spaces` types only | **[Direct]** Active; v1.2.3 released 2025-12-18 |
| PettingZoo AEC | **✅ SECONDARY: conformance wrapper + `api_test`** | **[Direct]** Active (v1.26.1); standard turn-based `agent_iter` / `last()` / `step()` API |
| Ray RLlib | **Reject for v1** | **[Direct]** "New API stack" introduced as alpha in Ray 2.10, replacing the old stack incrementally up to Ray 3.0 |
| RLCard | **Reject as a dependency** | **[Direct]** Repository activity in search results stops around 2023 |
| OpenSpiel | Optional stretch | **[Direct]** Active (v2.0.1); n-player imperfect-information games, C++ core with Python bindings |

```
                    ┌──────────────────────────┐
                    │  TarneebEngine (pure)    │   ← no torch, no gym, no I/O
                    │  deterministic, seeded    │   ← emits PublicEvent stream
                    └───────────┬───────────────┘
             ┌──────────────────┼──────────────────┐
             ▼                  ▼                  ▼
   ┌──────────────────┐ ┌───────────────┐ ┌────────────────┐
   │ VecTarneeb       │ │ TarneebAECEnv │ │ MatchSession   │
   │ N envs, masks,   │ │ conformance   │ │ 1 human + 3 AI │
   │ per-seat actor   │ │ + interop     │ │ per-seat actor │
   │ AND critic state │ │               │ │ state          │
   └──────────────────┘ └───────────────┘ └────────────────┘
```

`tarneeb.core` must never import `torch`, `gymnasium`, `pettingzoo`, `fastapi` or `streamlit`. Enforce with a test that inspects `sys.modules`.

### 4.2 Card encoding

```python
# tarneeb/core/cards.py
Suit = int   # 0=♣, 1=♦, 2=♥, 3=♠
Rank = int   # 0=2 ... 12=A
Card = int   # 0..51, card = suit * 13 + rank
def suit_of(c: Card) -> Suit: return c // 13
def rank_of(c: Card) -> Rank: return c % 13
def card_id(s: Suit, r: Rank) -> Card: return s * 13 + r
```

Hands are `int` bitmasks in the hot path; `list[Card]` views exist for the UI only.

### 4.3 PublicEvent — the canonical history record

```python
# tarneeb/core/events.py
EVENT_SCHEMA_VERSION = "event_v1"

class EventType(IntEnum):
    PAD = 0; BID = 1; PASS = 2; TRUMP_SELECTED = 3
    CARD_PLAYED = 4; TRICK_COMPLETED = 5; DEAL_COMPLETED = 6

@dataclass(frozen=True, slots=True)
class PublicEvent:
    seq: int                       # 0-based, monotonic and contiguous within a deal
    phase: Phase
    actor_seat: int | None         # ABSOLUTE seat; None for TRICK_/DEAL_COMPLETED
    event_type: EventType
    bid_value: int | None          # 7..13, only for BID
    trump: int | None              # 0..3, only for TRUMP_SELECTED
    card: Card | None              # 0..51, only for CARD_PLAYED
    trick_no: int                  # 0..12 during PLAY; 13 on DEAL_COMPLETED; 0 in BID/DECLARE
    trick_winner_seat: int | None  # only on TRICK_COMPLETED
    deal_result: DealResult | None # only on DEAL_COMPLETED (bid, tricks, ΔS — all public)
```

**Invariant EV-1: a `PublicEvent` never contains a card that is not already public.** `card` is populated only for `CARD_PLAYED`, a card just placed face-up. No field can carry a hand. Enforced by test T-E4, not by convention.

**Relativization.**

```python
def relativize(ev: PublicEvent, observer_seat: int) -> RelPublicEvent:
    """actor_rel: 0=self, 1=right-hand opponent, 2=partner, 3=left-hand opponent."""
    rel = None if ev.actor_seat is None else (ev.actor_seat - observer_seat) % 4
    win = None if ev.trick_winner_seat is None else (ev.trick_winner_seat - observer_seat) % 4
    return RelPublicEvent(seq=ev.seq, event_type=ev.event_type, actor_rel=rel,
                          bid_value=ev.bid_value, trump=ev.trump, card=ev.card,
                          trick_no=ev.trick_no, winner_rel=win, phase=ev.phase)
```

**Emission order.** Events are appended inside `step()` before it returns. A `CARD_PLAYED` completing a trick is emitted **before** its `TRICK_COMPLETED`. `DEAL_COMPLETED` follows the final `TRICK_COMPLETED`. `seq` resets to 0 at each new deal.

### 4.5 Determinism and seeding

One `numpy.random.Generator` per environment. Never the global RNG, never `random`.

```python
deal_seed = int.from_bytes(
    hashlib.sha256(f"{match_seed}:{deal_index}".encode()).digest()[:8], "big") % (2**63)
```

`deal(match_seed, deal_index)` is a pure function, which is what makes duplicate-deal evaluation (§12) possible.

### 4.6 Invariants

| # | Invariant | Test type |
|---|---|---|
| I1 | Deck is exactly 52 unique cards; the 4 hands are disjoint and cover it | property |
| I2 | `popcount(hand) + cards_played_by_seat == 13` always | property |
| I3 | If a player holds the led suit, every legal action is of that suit | property |
| I4 | Trick winner correct across all trump configurations | table unit |
| I5 | Auction terminates in ≤10 actions; exactly 1,823 sequences; 2,528 decision nodes | exhaustive |
| I6 | Scoring matches the hand-written 98-row truth table | table unit |
| I7 | `static_actor(s, seat)` is byte-identical across states differing only in other players' hands | **leakage** |
| I8 | Same seed ⇒ byte-identical action sequence, event stream and final score | determinism |
| I9 | 100,000 random-legal games: zero exceptions, zero illegal actions | fuzz |
| I10 | `pettingzoo.test.api_test` and `seed_test` pass | API compliance |
| I11 | Throughput ≥ measured target | benchmark |
| I12 | `ReplayEngine.verify` True for 10,000 deals, including event-stream equality | round-trip |
| I13 | Action 64 illegal in every reachable state; never sampled; zero gradient | property |
| I14 | `len(state.events) ≤ 77`; `seq` 0-based, contiguous, monotone | property |
| **I15** | **Every public event is consumed exactly once per (env, seat, policy instance) during rollout, and exactly once during reconstruction of its PPO chunk (§10.1)** | **accounting + replay** |
| **I16** | **`max_j \|Δ_s(j)\| ≤ K_MAX = 16` over exhaustive auctions and ≥10⁶ randomized deals** | property (§4.8) |

### 4.7 Event-system tests

| ID | Test | Assertion |
|---|---|---|
| **T-E1** | Ordered bidding events preserved | For 10,000 random auctions, the sub-sequence of `BID`/`PASS` events with `(actor_seat, bid_value)` exactly equals the executed auction. Nothing dropped, merged or reordered |
| **T-E2** | **Distinguishability (corrected in v1.2)** | See below |
| **T-E3** | Correct relative seat per observer | For every event and observer `o`, `relativize(ev,o).actor_rel == (ev.actor_seat − o) % 4`; a seat sees its own actions with `actor_rel == 0` |
| **T-E4** | No hidden cards in events | The multiset of `card` fields across `CARD_PLAYED` equals the 52 dealt cards; at index `k` the revealed set ⊆ cards played strictly before `k`; reflectively assert `PublicEvent` exposes no field that ever holds a hand bitmask |
| **T-E5** | **Chunk reconstruction is exact (rewritten in v1.2)** | See §10.1 and below |
| **T-E6** | **Per-(env, seat) independence for actor *and* critic states** | See below |
| **T-E7** | Reset boundary | With `gru_reset="deal"`, `h == 0` at the first decision of every deal including mid-match; with `"match"`, only at the first decision of the match. Pending event queues are empty immediately after every reset |
| **T-E8** | Replay reconstructs identical stream | `ReplayEngine.verify` compares every field of every event in order |
| **T-E9** | **`K_MAX` sufficiency (new)** | See §4.8 |
| **T-E10** | **Epoch-zero PPO ratio (new)** | See §10.5 |

**T-E2, corrected.** v1.1 required that two different auctions produce GRU hidden states separated by L2 > 1e-4. That is a property of a *particular trained or initialized network*, not a mathematical guarantee — a GRU may map two distinct inputs to arbitrarily close states, and a randomly initialized one certainly can. Asserting it as a unit-test invariant is wrong. T-E2 now asserts only what is guaranteed by construction:

1. Two auctions that differ in any bid, pass, actor or ordering produce **different raw `PublicEvent` sequences** (field-by-field comparison).
2. Their **factored-ID encodings differ**: the `(L, 7)` int arrays are not equal.
3. Their **padded feedforward tensors differ**: the `(80, 99)` one-hot expansions are not equal, and the difference occurs at an index where `hist_mask` is `True`.
4. **Order sensitivity:** reversing a non-symmetric event sub-sequence changes the ordered input at the encoding level (points 1–3 hold for the reversal too).

Whether the *trained* GRU actually exploits that distinction is an **empirical question measured by ablation A7**, not a unit test.

**T-E5, rewritten (chunk reconstruction exactness).** For 1,000 randomly generated chunks:
`replay_chunk(h0, prev_events[0..C-1])` produces, at every position `i`, a hidden state equal within `1e-5` to the state recorded live during rollout at that same decision. Two sub-assertions: `prev_events[0]` is empty (`ev_len[0] == 0`), and no event `seq` appears in more than one `prev_events[i]` of the same chunk.

**T-E6, extended to the critic.** Run `N = 8` envs. Assert (a) the 32 actor states and the 32 critic states are 64 distinct tensor slices; (b) mutating one does not change another; (c) seat `i`'s actor state after a deal equals the state obtained by replaying only seat `i`'s relativized stream; (d) the same holds for seat `i`'s **critic** state; (e) a partner's and an opponent's states in the same env are never equal to each other unless the underlying streams coincide.

**Framework mapping.** `pytest` for known-answer tests (I4, I5, I6, I10, I12, T-E1…T-E10 fixtures). `Hypothesis` for all-reachable-state invariants (I1, I2, I3, I7, I13, I14, I16, and the randomized halves of T-E2, T-E5, T-E9). Plain randomized loops for I9 and I11.

**The three highest-value tests are I7 (leakage), T-E5 (chunk exactness) and T-E10 (epoch-zero ratio).** Write I7 in week 4 and T-E5 + T-E10 in week 8 *before* the recurrent training loop.

### 4.8 Proving the event bound `K_MAX`

**Definition.** For seat `s`, let `Δ_s(j)` be the ordered list of public events from (and including) the first event produced by `s`'s decision `j`, up to but excluding the first event produced by `s`'s decision `j+1`. `K_MAX` must satisfy `|Δ_s(j)| ≤ K_MAX` for every seat, deal and `j`.

v1.1 set `K_MAX = 8` and justified it only from trick play. **That derivation was incomplete:** it ignored the case where a seat passes early in the auction and then does not act again until the first trick, during which the *entire rest of the auction*, the trump declaration, and up to three cards can occur.

**Complete derivation. [Derived]**

| Transition kind | Events in `Δ_s(j)` | Max | Reasoning |
|---|---|---|---|
| Bidding → next bidding decision by the same seat | own `BID`/`PASS`, then the other ≤3 active players' actions | **4** | The seat acts again after at most one full round of the ≤3 other active players |
| Bidding → DECLARE (seat is the declarer) | own final `BID`, then ≤3 `PASS` | **4** | The auction ends when the other three have passed |
| DECLARE → first card (declarer) | own `TRUMP_SELECTED`, then the declarer leads immediately | **1** | The declarer leads to trick 1 |
| **Bidding → first card (seat passed and is out)** | own `PASS`, then all remaining auction actions, then `TRUMP_SELECTED`, then ≤3 `CARD_PLAYED` before the seat | **14** | **The binding case.** See below |
| Trick play → next trick-play decision | own `CARD_PLAYED`, ≤3 more `CARD_PLAYED`, `TRICK_COMPLETED`, then ≤3 `CARD_PLAYED` of the next trick | **8** | Max at `p = 0` (seat leads) and `q = 3` (seat plays last next trick) |
| Final trick → deal end (terminal flush) | own `CARD_PLAYED`, ≤3 more, `TRICK_COMPLETED`, `DEAL_COMPLETED` | **6** | No subsequent decision in this episode; flushed, not stored |

**The binding case, verified by enumeration.** Over all 1,823 auction sequences, the maximum value of (a seat's own last auction action **plus** every auction event after it) is **10**, attained for example by:

```
seat 0: PASS
seat 1: BID 7 ; seat 2: BID 8 ; seat 3: BID 9
seat 1: BID 10; seat 2: BID 11; seat 3: BID 12
seat 1: BID 13; seat 2: PASS  ; seat 3: PASS      → declarer = seat 1
```

Seat 0's own `PASS` plus the nine subsequent auction events = 10. The declarer is seat 1, so the trick-1 order is 1, 2, 3, 0 and seat 0 plays **last**, with 3 `CARD_PLAYED` before it, plus the `TRUMP_SELECTED`:

```
|Δ| = 10 (auction, own action inclusive) + 1 (TRUMP_SELECTED) + 3 (cards) = 14
```

**Therefore `K_MAX = 14` is the true tight bound. This document sets `K_MAX = 16`** (nearest power of two, two events of headroom for a future optional variant such as `dealer_forced_seven`, which adds at most one forced action). The collector asserts `ev_len ≤ K_MAX` and raises immediately on violation.

**Deal boundaries never appear inside a `Δ`.** A deal boundary always forces a chunk boundary (§10.3), so no `Δ_s(j)` spans two deals. This keeps `K_MAX = 16` valid under **both** `gru_reset="deal"` and `gru_reset="match"`.

**T-E9 (property test).** (a) Enumerate all 1,823 auctions and assert the per-seat auction span never exceeds 10. (b) Simulate ≥10⁶ randomized legal deals, recording `max |Δ_s(j)|` over all seats and decisions; assert the observed maximum is ≤ 16 and **report it**; the test fails if it exceeds 14 (which would mean the derivation is wrong) or if the constructed witness above does not itself produce exactly 14. (c) Assert the pending-event queue for every seat is empty immediately after a deal reset.

---

## 5. Observation and Action Specification (`obs_v2`)

### 5.1 Five distinct information objects

| Object | Contains | Consumer | Rule |
|---|---|---|---|
| `TarneebState` | everything, including all 4 hands | engine only | never serialized whole |
| **`PublicEvent` stream** | the canonical ordered public record | actor history encoder, critic history encoder, UI, logger, replay | **contains no hidden card, ever (EV-1)** |
| `static_actor(s, seat)` | own hand + current public position | **actor at train and deploy** | invariant to other hands (I7) |
| `static_critic(s, seat)` | `static_actor` ∪ the other three hands ∪ derived counts | **critic at training only** | never loaded at inference |
| `PublicState` | JSON view for humans | UI, API | no hidden cards |

### 5.2 What v1.0 lost, and why the stream fixes it

`(high_bid, high_bidder, passed_set)` is not a sufficient statistic for the auction. `7 → 8 → 10 → 11` and `pass → pass → 11` both end at 11 but say very different things about where the strength sits. Likewise, the three cards played between your turns entered v1.0's network only through an order-free bag, discarding the signalling content of *which* card was chosen *when*. `obs_v2` makes the ordered event stream the primary history channel and keeps the flattened bags only as redundant order-free summaries that both model families receive equally.

### 5.3 Static feature table (`static_actor`, 692 dims)

Seat indices are **relative to the observer**: 0 = self, 1 = right-hand opponent, 2 = partner, 3 = left-hand opponent.

| # | Feature | Encoding | Dims | Actor | Critic | UI | Log |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| S01 | Own hand | multi-hot | 52 | ✔ | ✔ | ✔ | ✔ |
| S02 | Cards played, by relative seat | 4×52 multi-hot | 208 | ✔ | ✔ | ✔ | ✔ |
| S03 | Current trick, by relative seat | 4×52 one-hot | 208 | ✔ | ✔ | ✔ | ✔ |
| S04 | Unseen-card mask | multi-hot | 52 | ✔ | ✔ | ✘ | ✔ |
| S05 | Legal-action mask | bool | 65 | ✔ | ✔ | ✔ | ✔ |
| S06 | Void matrix (rel. seat × suit) | binary | 16 | ✔ | ✔ | ✔ | ✔ |
| S07 | Play order in trick + "am I leading" | one-hot + bit | 5 | ✔ | ✔ | ✔ | ✔ |
| S08 | Led suit (or none) | one-hot | 5 | ✔ | ✔ | ✔ | ✔ |
| S09 | Current high bid (or none) | one-hot | 8 | ✔ | ✔ | ✔ | ✔ |

| | **Total** | | **692** | | | | |

**Critic-only additions (164 dims → `D_CRITIC = 856`):**

| # | Feature | Encoding | Dims | Actor |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| X01 | The three hidden hands, by relative seat | 3×52 multi-hot | 156 | **✘ NEVER** |
| X02 | Trump count per relative seat | 4 scalars / 13 | 4 | **✘** |
| X03 | High-card count per relative seat | 4 scalars / 13 | 4 | **✘** |

`static_critic(s, seat)` is **relative to `seat`**, exactly like `static_actor`. This is why the critic needs per-seat recurrent state (§6.1).

### 5.4 Event feature encoding

Each event becomes **7 factored categorical ids**:

| Field | Cardinality | Values |
|---|---|---|
| `type` | 7 | PAD, BID, PASS, TRUMP_SELECTED, CARD_PLAYED, TRICK_COMPLETED, DEAL_COMPLETED |
| `actor_rel` | 5 | none, self, RHO, partner, LHO |
| `bid_value` | 8 | none, 7..13 |
| `trump` | 6 | none, ♣, ♦, ♥, ♠, NT (reserved) |
| `card` | 53 | none, 0..51 |
| `trick_no` | 15 | none, 0..13 |
| `winner_rel` | 5 | none, self, RHO, partner, LHO |
| | **99 one-hot dims** | |

- **Feedforward baseline:** one-hot concatenation → 99 floats per event.
- **Recurrent model:** embedding lookup per field (`type 16, actor_rel 8, bid 8, trump 8, card 32, trick_no 8, winner_rel 8`, sum 88) → `Linear(88→64)` → 64-dim event embedding.

Buffers store the compact `(·, 7)` int16 id array and expand to one-hot on device. This keeps buffer memory ~7× smaller than storing one-hot.

### 5.5 Padded history for the feedforward baseline

| Item | Value | Justification |
|---|---|---|
| `L_MAX` | **80** | 77 max events per deal, plus headroom |
| Padding | **Right-padding** with `type = PAD` and all other fields `none` | Left-padding would misalign "most recent event" across deals of different length |
| Padding mask | `hist_mask[80]` bool | Padded positions zeroed **after** the per-event linear so its bias cannot leak a constant |
| Stored shape | `hist_ids: (B, 80, 7)` int16; expanded to `(B, 80, 99)` float on device | |
| Coverage | The complete ordered auction (every `BID`/`PASS` with actor and value), `TRUMP_SELECTED`, every `CARD_PLAYED` in order, every `TRICK_COMPLETED` with winner | |

```
hist_ids (B,80,7) --one-hot--> (B,80,99)
                  --Linear(99→16)+ReLU--> (B,80,16)
                  --* mask.unsqueeze(-1)--> (B,80,16)
                  --flatten--> (B,1280)
                  --Linear(1280→256)+ReLU--> (B,256) = z_hist
```

Parameters: `99·16+16 = 1,600` plus `1280·256+256 = 327,936` = **329,536**.

**Comparability.** The recurrent history path costs `7,816 + 247,296 = 255,112` parameters. The FF path costs 329,536 — about 29% *more*. The FF baseline is therefore not capacity-handicapped, so a GRU win in ablation A1 cannot be explained by parameters. State this in the report.

### 5.6 Recurrent history encoder

Per seat `s`, maintain `h_s ∈ R^(1,1,256)` (actor) and `hc_s ∈ R^(1,1,256)` (critic). On every engine step that emits events `E`, all four seats consume `E` in order from their own relative perspective, batched into a single GRU call.

**The ordering rule, stated once and enforced everywhere:** *after `step()` returns, advance every seat's history state on the newly emitted events; then, at the next decision point, the acting seat uses its already-current state and consumes nothing further.* This is the convention formalized in §10.1.

**Cost. [Engineering judgement]** ~4× more GRU steps than an own-decisions-only design, mitigated by a 64-d input and batching all four seats into one `(k, 4·N, 64)` call. Budget 1.3–2× wall-clock on the rollout loop; measure in week 8.

**Reset boundary.**

| Config | Behaviour | Use |
|---|---|---|
| `gru_reset = "deal"` (**default**) | `h_s, hc_s ← 0` at the start of every deal, including mid-match; pending event queues cleared | Stages 1–11 |
| `gru_reset = "match"` | zero only at match start | Optional ablation at stage 11 |

**Recommendation for stage 11: keep `"deal"`.** Cross-deal context reaches the network through S18/S19. Cross-deal opponent modelling is a separate research question needing a separate slower recurrent layer. **[Engineering judgement]** In both modes a deal boundary forces a chunk boundary, so `K_MAX` and the §10.1 convention are unaffected.

### 5.7 Action space

Unified masked discrete, **65 actions**.

| ID range | Action | Phase | Legality |
|---|---|---|---|
| 0–51 | `CARD(c)` | PLAY | in hand ∧ (follows led suit ∨ void in led suit) |
| 52–58 | `BID(7)`…`BID(13)` | BID | `v > high_bid` ∧ seat active |
| 59 | `PASS` | BID | seat active |
| 60–63 | `TRUMP(♣/♦/♥/♠)` | DECLARE | seat is declarer |
| 64 | `TRUMP(NT)` | DECLARE | **permanently masked under `tarneeb-classic-v1`** |

One `Categorical` and one mask means trivial PPO log-prob bookkeeping, a rectangular buffer, one entropy term, and `MaskablePPO` compatibility for the week-6 baseline.

## 6. Neural Network Architecture

### 6.1 Three-part structure, and why the critic is per-seat

```
                 ┌───────────────────────────┐
   static_actor  │  1. STATIC ENCODER        │
   (B, 692) ────►│  Linear 692→512 +LN+ReLU  │──► z_static (B,256)
                 │  Linear 512→256 +LN+ReLU  │        │
                 └───────────────────────────┘        │
                                                      ├─► 3. FUSION
   relativized   ┌───────────────────────────┐        │   cat(512)
   PublicEvent ─►│  2. HISTORY ENCODER       │──►     │   Linear 512→256 +ReLU
   stream        │  (a) GRU path, or         │  z_hist│   Linear 256→256 +ReLU
                 │  (b) padded-FF path       │ (B,256)│        │
                 └───────────────────────────┘        │        └─► actor head 256→65 →mask
                                                      │
   (separate network, identical shape, input static_critic (B,856))
                                                      └─► critic head 256→1
```

**Actor and critic are entirely separate networks: separate static encoders, separate embedding tables, separate GRUs, separate fusion.** No shared parameters. This is the structural guarantee that the critic's privileged input cannot reach the policy, and it also means the critic's recurrent state is its own object.

**Per-seat critic state (corrected in v1.2).** `static_critic(state, seat)` is expressed **relative to `seat`**: X01 lists the three hidden hands ordered as (RHO, partner, LHO) *from that seat's viewpoint*, and the critic's history encoder consumes `relativize(ev, seat)`. A single critic state per environment would therefore be fed a sequence whose relative-seat labels change meaning whenever the acting seat changes — seat 0's stream calls seat 2 "partner" while seat 1's stream calls seat 2 "LHO". Folding both into one hidden vector mixes incompatible coordinate frames and produces a value estimate conditioned on an incoherent history.

```
hc.shape = (n_envs, 4, 1, hidden_size)      # was (n_envs, 1, hidden_size) in v1.1
```

When a learner-controlled seat `a` acts in env `e`, the critic uses `static_critic(state, a)` together with `hc[e, a]`. Critic history is advanced for **all four seats** in every environment after every engine step. Advancing all four unconditionally, rather than only the learner-controlled ones, costs one extra batched GRU call per step and removes an entire class of bugs that would appear the moment league seating changes which seats are learner-controlled. **[Engineering judgement]**

**The rejected alternative, and why.** A *team-level* critic state — one per (env, team) — is only coherent if the critic uses **seat-absolute** encoding (absolute seat ids, no relativization). That design is defensible in isolation: it halves the critic's recurrent work and gives both partners literally the same value function input history. It is rejected here for two reasons. First, it breaks symmetry with the actor: the actor is seat-relative because that is what makes one shared policy valid in all four seats, and a seat-absolute critic would have to learn four separate positional conventions from the same data, undoing the 4× data multiplier. Second, the advantage `A_t = R_t − V(s_t)` is computed per seat; a team-shared `V` would give both partners identical baselines and remove exactly the per-seat variance reduction that motivates a centralized critic in the first place. If you want to test it anyway, it is a clean addition to ablation A6 — but specify it as *seat-absolute*, never as "relative but shared".

### 6.2 Layer-by-layer, recurrent configuration

```
ACTOR (recurrent)
  inputs  static        (B, 692)   float32
          prev_ev_ids   (B, K, 7)  int16     # K <= K_MAX = 16; empty at a chunk head
          prev_ev_len   (B,)       int32
          legal_mask    (B, 65)    bool
          h_in          (1, B, 256) float32
  ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  A1  Linear(692 → 512) + LayerNorm(512) + ReLU     (B, 512)
  A2  Linear(512 → 256) + LayerNorm(256) + ReLU     (B, 256)   = z_static
  E1  7 embedding tables → concat                   (B, K, 88)
  E2  Linear(88 → 64) + ReLU                        (B, K, 64)
  E3  GRU(input=64, hidden=256, layers=1)           h_out (1,B,256); z_hist = h_out[0]
      (no-op where prev_ev_len == 0)
  F1  concat(z_static, z_hist)                      (B, 512)
  F2  Linear(512 → 256) + ReLU                      (B, 256)
  F3  Linear(256 → 256) + ReLU                      (B, 256)
  P1  Linear(256 → 65)                              (B, 65)  logits
  P2  logits.masked_fill(~legal_mask, finfo.min)    → Categorical

CRITIC (recurrent, training only, SEPARATE parameters, PER-SEAT state)
  inputs  critic_static (B, 856); prev_ev_ids; prev_ev_len; hc_in (1,B,256)
  ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  C1  Linear(856 → 512) + LayerNorm(512) + ReLU
  C2  Linear(512 → 256) + LayerNorm(256) + ReLU     = z_static_c
  CE  own embedding tables + Linear(88→64) + ReLU
  CG  GRU(64, 256)                                  hc_out; z_hist_c
  CF  concat → Linear(512→256)+ReLU → Linear(256→256)+ReLU
  CV  Linear(256 → 1)                               V(s)
```

Feedforward configuration: replace `E1..E3` / `CE..CG` with the §5.5 block taking `hist_ids (B,80,7)` and `hist_mask (B,80)`; everything else identical, and no recurrent state exists.

### 6.3 Parameter counts — recomputed in v1.2 including LayerNorm and GRU biases

v1.1's totals omitted the trainable `LayerNorm` weight and bias. Each `LayerNorm(d)` with `elementwise_affine=True` contributes `2d` parameters: `LayerNorm(512) = 1,024`, `LayerNorm(256) = 512`. Each static encoder therefore gains 1,536 parameters. PyTorch's `nn.GRU` with `bias=True` contributes `3H·I + 3H·H + 3H + 3H` (both `bias_ih` and `bias_hh`), which the v1.1 formula already included.

**Mandatory verification snippet.** Add this as `tests/test_param_counts.py`; it must run in CI and fail on any drift, which is what keeps §6.3 from silently rotting as you edit `nets.py`.

```python
EXPECTED = {
    ("gru", "actor"):    956_617,
    ("gru", "critic"): 1_024_137,
    ("ff",  "actor"):  1_031_041,
    ("ff",  "critic"): 1_098_561,
}

def count(m): return sum(p.numel() for p in m.parameters())

@pytest.mark.parametrize("hist", ["gru", "ff"])
def test_parameter_counts(hist):
    arch = dict(static_dim=692, critic_dim=856, hidden=256, d_event=64,
                l_max=80, k_max=16, n_actions=65, history_encoder=hist)
    a, c = ActorNet(**arch), CriticNet(**arch)
    assert count(a) == EXPECTED[(hist, "actor")]
    assert count(c) == EXPECTED[(hist, "critic")]
    # structural guarantee: no shared parameters between actor and critic
    assert {id(p) for p in a.parameters()}.isdisjoint({id(p) for p in c.parameters()})
```

### 6.4 Architecture comparison and progression

| Architecture | History handling | History params | Impl. risk | Verdict |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **Flattened MLP + padded event block** | Full ordered history, order-aware via flattened position | 329,536 | Low | **Stages 1–7. Ship first** |
| **GRU over events** | Full ordered history, learned recurrence, incremental | 255,112 | Medium (state management) | **✅ PRIMARY, stage 8+** |
| **LSTM over events** | as GRU | ~330k | Medium+ | Marginal on ≤77-step sequences. Use GRU |
| **Transformer over events** | Attention over the whole record | ~500k+ | High | **Optional extension**; attention maps make a good interpretability figure |

### 6.5 Pseudocode

```python
def encode_events(ev_ids, ev_len, tables, proj):
    """ev_ids: (B, K, 7) int; PAD rows are all-zero ids."""
    parts = [tables[i](ev_ids[..., i]) for i in range(7)]      # 7 x (B,K,d_i)
    x = torch.cat(parts, dim=-1)                               # (B, K, 88)
    x = F.relu(proj(x))                                        # (B, K, 64)
    valid = torch.arange(x.size(1), device=x.device)[None, :] < ev_len[:, None]
    return x * valid.unsqueeze(-1)


def advance_history(gru, tables, proj, ev_ids, ev_len, h):
    """Consume ev_len events for a batch of (env, seat) slots. h: (1, B, 256).
    Rows with ev_len == 0 are returned unchanged — this is what makes the
    chunk-head transition a strict no-op (§10.1)."""
    if int(ev_len.max()) == 0:
        return h
    x = encode_events(ev_ids, ev_len, tables, proj)
    packed = nn.utils.rnn.pack_padded_sequence(
        x, ev_len.cpu().clamp(min=1), batch_first=True, enforce_sorted=False)
    _, h_out = gru(packed, h)
    keep = (ev_len == 0).view(1, -1, 1)
    return torch.where(keep, h, h_out)


def actor_forward(static, prev_ev_ids, prev_ev_len, mask, h_in):
    """h_in is the state at the PREVIOUS decision (or the stored chunk head).
    prev_ev_* are the events strictly between that decision and this one.
    At a chunk head prev_ev_len == 0 and h_in is used unchanged."""
    h = advance_history(a_gru, a_tables, a_proj, prev_ev_ids, prev_ev_len, h_in)
    z = a_fusion(torch.cat([a_static_enc(static), h[0]], dim=-1))
    logits = a_policy_head(z).masked_fill(~mask, torch.finfo(torch.float32).min)
    return logits, h


def critic_forward(critic_static, prev_ev_ids, prev_ev_len, hc_in):
    hc = advance_history(c_gru, c_tables, c_proj, prev_ev_ids, prev_ev_len, hc_in)
    z = c_fusion(torch.cat([c_static_enc(critic_static), hc[0]], dim=-1))
    return c_value_head(z).squeeze(-1), hc


def masked_action(logits, mask, deterministic=False, temperature=1.0):
    assert mask.any(dim=-1).all(), "state with zero legal actions"
    dist = torch.distributions.Categorical(logits=logits / temperature)
    a = logits.argmax(-1) if deterministic else dist.sample()
    return a, dist.log_prob(a), dist.entropy()
```

Use `torch.finfo(dtype).min`, not `-1e9`. **[Direct]** SB3-contrib logged a bug where `MaskableCategorical.apply_masking()` crashed with a Simplex `ValueError` when cached probabilities deviated from sum=1 in float32 with large action spaces.

Note the signature change from v1.1: `actor_forward` no longer takes a `new_deal` flag. Resets are handled by the collector at the deal boundary (§10.2 step 0) rather than inside the network, because a reset must also clear the pending-event queue, which the network cannot see.

### 6.6 Hidden-state rules

| Situation | Rule |
|---|---|
| Rollout, actor | `h: (n_envs, 4, 1, 256)` — one slot per (env, seat) |
| Rollout, critic | `hc: (n_envs, 4, 1, 256)` — **one slot per (env, seat)** (corrected in v1.2) |
| Every engine step | Advance **all four seats** of both `h` and `hc` on the newly emitted events, batched, immediately after `step()` returns |
| Decision point | The acting seat uses `h[e, a]` / `hc[e, a]` **as-is**, consuming nothing |
| Deal boundary | Flush trailing events, then zero all four `h` and `hc` slots of that env, then clear all four pending-event queues, then start a new chunk |
| League opponent acts | That seat's actor state belongs to *that policy's* parameters. Keyed `(env, seat, policy_id)`. When seating changes, the state is re-created |
| PPO update | Restore `h0`/`hc0` at the chunk head; reconstruct forward per §10.1 |
| Deployment | `MatchSession` holds `dict[seat, Tensor]` for the actor only; reset per deal |

Attach a debug tag `(deal_index, last_seq_consumed)` to every hidden state and assert it matches the engine before every forward pass. This single assertion catches nearly every recurrent bug in this project.

### 6.9 Why the critic may cheat and the actor may not

$$\nabla_\theta J = \mathbb{E}\big[\nabla_\theta \log \pi_\theta(a_t \mid o_t)\, A_t\big], \qquad A_t = R_t - V(s_t)$$

The baseline enters only through the **scalar** `A_t`. Any state-dependent baseline leaves the gradient's expectation unbiased while reducing variance. The actor is conditioned on `o_t` alone, which is exactly what the deployed agent can use.

**[Inferred]** Suphx runs the aggressive version: an oracle agent sees other players' private tiles and the wall, and the perfect information is progressively removed during training. A centralized critic is the mild, standard form.

The one real danger is a gradient path from the critic into the actor. §6.1 forbids shared parameters and `test_param_counts.py` asserts parameter-id disjointness. Ablation A6 measures how much each privileged block contributes.

## 7. Reward System

### 7.1 Options compared

| Design | Sparsity | Credit assignment | Bidding effect | Verdict |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Match win/loss | very sparse (~600 decisions) | very hard | correct but unlearnable early | fine-tune only |
| Deal win/loss | sparse (~17 decisions) | hard | ignores margin | weak |
| Raw Tarneeb score | sparse | medium | correct | unnormalized |
| **Team score difference** | sparse (terminal) | medium | **correct incentives** | **✅ PRIMARY** |
| Contract-success bonus | dense-ish | medium | encourages underbidding | component only |
| Per-trick shaping | dense | easy | **damages bidding** | stages 2–4 only |
| Potential-based shaping | dense | easy | **policy-invariant under stated assumptions** | ✅ safe densification |

### 7.2 Stage reward A — deal-level, primary, stages 5–10

For a player on team `k`:

$$r_T = \frac{\Delta S_k - \Delta S_{1-k}}{42}, \qquad r_t = 0 \ \text{for}\ t < T$$

Range exactly `[-1, +1]` by §2.6. Both partners receive the **identical** reward; both opponents receive its negation, so `r_{team0} = -r_{team1}` exactly. `γ = 1.0` within a deal.

*Alternative:* `Δ/13` clipped to `[-3, 3]`. Because PPO normalizes advantages, the scale mainly affects the value-loss coefficient balance. Pick one, record it, never change it mid-experiment.

### 7.3 Stage reward B — match-level, stage 11, with corrected shaping

**Episode definition.** In stage 11 an episode is one **match**: it begins at deal 0 with `match_score = (0, 0)` and ends the moment a team reaches `target_score`. Deals within a match are *not* episode boundaries for the reward, though they remain chunk and recurrent-reset boundaries.

**Terminal reward.**

$$r_T = +1 \ \text{(match won by my team)} \quad\text{or}\quad -1 \ \text{(lost)}$$

**Shaping potential.** Let `s_d` denote the post-deal state after deal `d`, with match scores `(m_mine, m_theirs)`.

$$
\Phi(s) =
\begin{cases}
0 & \text{if } s \text{ is terminal}\\[4pt]
\beta \tanh\!\Big(\dfrac{m_{\text{mine}} - m_{\text{theirs}}}{\tau}\Big) & \text{otherwise}
\end{cases}
\qquad \beta = 0.5,\ \tau = 12
$$

**`Φ(terminal) = 0` is not cosmetic.** Ng, Harada & Russell's policy-invariance result for episodic tasks requires the potential to vanish at the absorbing terminal state; without it the shaping adds a nonzero constant to terminal returns that depends on *which* terminal state was reached, which can change the optimal policy. v1.1 omitted this and its shaping was therefore **not** guaranteed policy-invariant. Corrected here.

**Shaping term, applied at each deal boundary.**

$$F(s_d, s_{d+1}) = \gamma\,\Phi(s_{d+1}) - \Phi(s_d), \qquad \gamma = 1.0$$

**Telescoping. [Derived]** Over a complete match with deals `d = 0 … D−1`, `s_0` the initial state and `s_D` terminal:

$$\sum_{d=0}^{D-1} F(s_d, s_{d+1}) \;=\; \sum_{d=0}^{D-1}\big[\Phi(s_{d+1}) - \Phi(s_d)\big] \;=\; \Phi(s_D) - \Phi(s_0) \;=\; 0 - \Phi(s_0)$$

and `Φ(s_0) = β·tanh(0) = 0` because every match starts 0–0. **Therefore the total shaping contribution to any complete episode return is exactly 0.** Shaping only *redistributes* return across deals; it never changes any episode's total. This is the strongest possible form of the guarantee and it is worth stating in the report.

**Assumptions required for the policy-invariance claim, stated in full.** Do not claim invariance without all five:

1. `γ` is the same in the shaping term and in the return. Here both are `1.0`.
2. `Φ` is a function of state only — not of the action, the policy, the opponent's identity, or the timestep. Here it depends only on `match_score`, which is part of the state (S18/S19).
3. `Φ(terminal) = 0`.
4. The episode is the full match, and `F` is applied at every deal boundary within it, never skipped.
5. **[Inferred, and the weakest link]** The original result is proved for single-agent MDPs. Tarneeb is a two-team POSG. The natural extension requires the shaping to be applied *consistently to every learning agent* and to be seat-relative in the same way the reward is, so that `F_{team0} = −F_{team1}`. Our `Φ` satisfies this because `m_mine − m_theirs` negates under team swap and `tanh` is odd. I have **not** re-verified the multi-agent theorem in this session; treat the multi-agent invariance as a reasoned extension, not a cited proof, and note it as such in the report.

**Practical check to run once (T-R1):** on 1,000 simulated complete matches with a fixed random policy, assert that `sum(r_t + F_t) == sum(r_t)` to within `1e-6`. If it does not, one of assumptions 1–4 is violated in your implementation.

### 7.4 Stage reward C — curriculum stages 2–4 only, then deleted

`+0.05` per trick won, `−0.05` per trick lost. Delete before stage 5.

### 7.5 The four questions

**Sparse rewards.** Mitigations by value: short episodes, a strong centralized critic, GAE with `λ < 1`, potential-based shaping. **[Inferred]** Suphx solved the same round-vs-game boundary with a learned global reward predictor mapping current and previous round information to the final reward. Training a small deal-value predictor as `Φ` is an excellent optional extension — but note it would break assumption 2 above unless it is a pure function of the public state, so keep the learned predictor frozen during the RL run.

**Partner credit assignment.** Shared team reward, shared parameters, same deal-level signal for both partners. Mitigations: the per-seat centralized critic (each partner's `V` differs because their observations, event streams and hidden states differ — this is a second, independent reason for §6.1's per-seat state) and role-split evaluation metrics. Do not attempt COMA-style counterfactual baselines in v1.

**Why excessive trick rewards damage bidding.** If a trick is worth `+w` unconditionally, bidding 11 and taking 10 costs `−11` while taking 10 tricks pays `+10w`. The agent learns "tricks good, contracts risky" and collapses to passing. Signature: mean bid → 7, pass rate > 60%, contract success > 95%. The fix is to delete the trick reward, not tune `w`.

**Why masking, not punishment.** A `−1` illegal-action penalty makes the agent spend a million steps learning rules you already know, and the deployed model can still emit an illegal action. Masking makes them impossible and costs nothing. Track illegal-action rate anyway: it must be exactly 0.0.

**Discount and the delayed bid.** A bid at `t=0` resolves at `t≈17` (deal) or `t≈600` (match). At `γ=0.99` with `T−t=600`, the factor is `0.99^600 ≈ 0.0024` — no signal. Deal episodes use `γ = 1.0`; match episodes use `γ = 1.0` with the shaping above. Never `γ = 0.99`.

## 8. Curriculum

| # | Stage | Enabled | Partners / opponents | Reward | Objective | Minimum success criterion (**target, not result**) | Advance when | Failure signs |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Legal random play | Full engine + event stream, no learning | Random ×4 | none | Validate engine | 100k games, 0 crashes, 0 illegal; I1–I16 and T-E1…T-E9 green | all tests green | any exception; nonzero illegal rate |
| 2 | Trick play only | Fixed trump ♠, fixed contract 8, no auction | Random ×3 | C | Learn follow-suit value | Win rate vs random ≥ 70% | ≥70% over 5k deals | flat curve → check mask/obs wiring |
| 3 | Fixed trump + contract | Deal reward | Random ×3, then heuristic-basic ×3 | A | Learn contract play | Beat heuristic-basic ≥ 52% | CI excludes 50% | reward stuck at 0 → critic not learning |
| 4 | Random trump + contract | Trump and contract sampled | heuristic-basic ×3 | A | Generalize | Contract success ≥ 60% when declaring | stable over 3 evals | varies by trump → relative-seat bug |
| 5 | Rule-based opponents | Full play phase | heuristic-strong ×3 | A | Match a competent opponent | Score diff ≥ −0.5 pts/deal | plateau | large negative → return to stage 4 |
| 6 | Full bidding | Auction on, action 64 masked | heuristic-strong ×3 | A | Learn to bid | Beat heuristic-strong ≥ 53%; bid-calibration slope 0.6–1.4 | ≥53% with CI | pass rate >70% or contract success <45% |
| 7 | Ordered-history validation | FF padded-history baseline to convergence | heuristic-strong ×3 | A | Confirm the baseline uses ordered auction history | T-E2 passes; **A7** shows removing auction events degrades E3 by ≥0.2 pts/deal | A7 shows a real dependence | no degradation → model ignoring history; check padded-row zeroing |
| 8 | Current-policy self-play | 4 copies of the learner (mirror + four-copy) | self | A | Beyond the heuristic ceiling | **T-E5 and T-E10 green before any training**; beats the stage-6 checkpoint ≥ 55% | 2 consecutive promotions | E3 drops while self-play rises → convention collapse |
| 9 | Historical league | PFSP over snapshots (§9) | league | A | Robustness, anti-cycling | Beats every frozen snapshot ≥52%; beats heuristic-strong ≥58% | 3 promotions, no regression | cyclic payoff matrix |
| 10 | Diverse partners | Cross-seed partner slice enabled | mixed | A | Human compatibility | Cross-play score ≥ 80% of self-play score | stable | XP/SP < 0.6 → private conventions |
| 11 | Full-match training | Episode = match to 31; reward B with `Φ(terminal)=0`; `gru_reset` still "deal" | league | B | Score-aware bidding | **T-R1 green**; match win rate vs stage-10 ≥ 53% | plateau | value loss explodes → check the telescoping |
| 12 | Human evaluation | Deployment | you + friends | none | Qualitative | ≥30 deals with 3+ humans, structured feedback | project end | "bids nonsense" → revisit stage 6 |

Stages 1–7 are the MVP. Stages 8–12 are the research system. Every advance uses a paired duplicate-deal comparison with a bootstrap CI (§12), never a raw TensorBoard reading.

## 9. Self-Play, League Seating and Gradient Ownership

### 9.1 Policy architecture

| Option | Verdict |
|---|---|
| **One shared policy usable in all four seats** | **✅ Base**, enabled by relative-seat encoding. Up to 4× data per update |
| Separate declarer / partner / defender policies | **Reject.** Role is already in S14; splitting discards data |
| Population of independent policies | ✅ For stage-10 partner diversity and cross-play evaluation, 3–4 seeds |
| Historical frozen snapshots | **✅ Core of the league** |

### 9.2 The complete seating procedure (new in v1.2)

v1.1 described random seat assignment, mirror/snapshot/cross-seed partners, and four-copy self-play without saying how they compose. Here is the full procedure, executed **once per deal, per environment**, before the deal is dealt.

```python
def sample_seating(rng, league, cfg) -> Seating:
    """Returns, for each of the 4 seats: the controlling policy id and whether
    that seat's transitions are gradient-eligible for the shared actor."""

    # 1. Which partnership is the LEARNING TEAM this deal?
    L = rng.choice([(0, 2), (1, 3)])          # learning partnership
    O = (1, 3) if L == (0, 2) else (0, 2)     # opposing partnership

    # 2. Which self-play / partner mode?
    mode = rng.choice(["four_copy", "mirror", "snapshot", "cross_seed"],
                      p=[cfg.p_four_copy,     # 0.10
                         cfg.p_mirror,        # 0.50
                         cfg.p_snapshot,      # 0.30
                         cfg.p_cross_seed])   # 0.10

    policy = {}; grad = {}

    if mode == "four_copy":
        # Pure self-play: the CURRENT learner occupies all four seats.
        for s in range(4): policy[s], grad[s] = LEARNER, True
        return Seating(policy, grad, learning_team=L, mode=mode)

    # 3. Learning partnership
    if mode == "mirror":
        for s in L: policy[s], grad[s] = LEARNER, True
    else:
        k = rng.integers(2)                    # which of the two seats the learner takes
        policy[L[k]],     grad[L[k]]     = LEARNER, True
        partner_pool = league.snapshots if mode == "snapshot" else league.cross_seed_pool
        policy[L[1-k]],   grad[L[1-k]]   = league.sample(partner_pool, pfsp=False), False

    # 4. Opponents: ONE league member controls BOTH opposing seats,
    #    so the opposition is a coherent partnership rather than two strangers.
    opp = league.sample_pfsp()                 # §9.3 weights
    for s in O: policy[s], grad[s] = opp, False

    return Seating(policy, grad, learning_team=L, mode=mode)
```

**Per-deal specification, as required:**

| Question | Answer |
|---|---|
| Which partnership is the learning team? | Uniformly `{0,2}` or `{1,3}`, redrawn every deal |
| Which seats use the current learner? | `four_copy`: all four. `mirror`: both seats of the learning partnership. `snapshot`/`cross_seed`: exactly one randomly chosen seat of the learning partnership |
| Which seat may use a frozen partner? | The other seat of the learning partnership, in `snapshot` and `cross_seed` modes only |
| Which policy controls each opponent? | A **single** league member, PFSP-sampled, controls **both** opposing seats. Overridden only by an explicitly documented diversity experiment, which must set `cfg.heterogeneous_opponents = True` and be recorded in the run config |
| Which actions receive actor gradients? | Exactly those from seats with `grad[s] == True`, i.e. seats controlled by the *current* learner. Frozen partners and all opponents contribute **no** actor gradient |
| Which rewards and value targets go to each learner-controlled seat? | Each gradient-eligible seat `s` receives `r = (ΔS_{team(s)} − ΔS_{1−team(s)}) / 42`, i.e. **its own team's perspective**, and a value target computed from `static_critic(state, s)` with `hc[env, s]` |

**Zero-sum bookkeeping. [Derived]** By construction `r_{team0} = −r_{team1}` for every deal. In `four_copy` mode both teams are the same shared policy and receive exactly opposite rewards; both feed the same actor. This is correct and is standard parameter sharing: the shared policy is trained to maximize *the return of whichever team it is currently seated in*, and because seat assignment is symmetric and redrawn every deal, the expected gradient is well defined. It is **not** a bug that the two halves of a four-copy deal push in opposite directions — they are different observations paired with opposite advantages, which is exactly the signal that teaches the policy to play both sides.

**Critic indexing, restated.** For every gradient-eligible seat `s` in env `e`: input `static_critic(state, s)`, recurrent state `hc[e, s]`, target `R̂` from that seat's own reward stream. Never `hc[e, partner_of(s)]`, never a team-shared state (§6.1).

**Sampling proportions.** The four modes above replace v1.1's split between "opponent sampling" and "partner sampling", which were specified independently and could not be composed. `p_four_copy = 0.10`, `p_mirror = 0.50`, `p_snapshot = 0.30`, `p_cross_seed = 0.10` (the last enabled from stage 10 onward; before then its mass is added to `p_snapshot`).

### 9.3 Opponent PFSP weights

**[Inferred]** Structure follows AlphaStar's league, where main agents use prioritized fictitious self-play with mixture probabilities adapted to opponent win rates. Simplified: no separate exploiter agents in v1.

| League member (opponent pool) | Base share |
|---|---|
| Current champion | 30% |
| Recent snapshots (last 5) | 35%, PFSP-weighted |
| Older diverse snapshots (≤10, reservoir) | 22%, PFSP-weighted |
| heuristic-strong (fixed anchor) | 9% |
| random-legal (sanity anchor) | 4% |

PFSP weight for opponent `o` with win rate `p_o`: `w_o ∝ (1 − p_o)^α`, `α = 2`, `p_o` an EMA over the last 500 deals. (The current learner does not appear in the *opponent* pool; self-play against the learner is expressed by `four_copy` mode in §9.2.)

### 9.4 Seat rotation and deal duplication

- **Seat rotation** is subsumed by §9.2: the learning partnership and, in snapshot/cross-seed modes, the specific seat, are redrawn every deal.
- **Deal duplication (evaluation only):** every deal seed is played twice with team assignments swapped. Highest-leverage variance reduction available.
- **Never duplicate deals in training rollouts** — it correlates samples within a batch.

### 9.5 Snapshots, promotion, forgetting, cycles

| Item | Policy |
|---|---|
| Snapshot frequency | every 2M environment steps or 50 updates, whichever first |
| Promotion gate | candidate beats champion over **≥2,000 duplicated deals**, bootstrap 95% CI on mean paired score difference strictly above 0, **and** does not lose to any of the last 5 snapshots, **and** beats heuristic-strong |
| Retaining weak-but-diverse checkpoints | reservoir-sample by **behavioural fingerprint** (mean bid, pass rate, contract success, trick-1 trump-lead rate, mean trick index of first trump play, mean observed auction length, …). Keep if minimum L2 distance to all archived fingerprints exceeds a threshold, even at low Elo |
| Cycle detection | maintain cross-play payoff matrix `M`; check `M − Mᵀ` for 3-cycles; report the count per run |
| Limiting forgetting | ≥22% older-snapshot share; the no-regression promotion gate; a fixed held-out suite of 2,000 deal seeds never used in training |
| PPO data reuse | data collected under the current learner's parameters may be reused for `n_epochs` passes. Transitions from non-gradient-eligible seats contribute **no** actor gradient and **no** value target. Never reuse a batch across parameter updates beyond the epoch loop. **[Inferred]** MAPPO found high data reuse detrimental in multi-agent settings — start at **4–5** epochs, not 10 |

### 9.6 Cooperating with a human whose style differs

1. **Partner diversity in training** (stage 10, `cross_seed` mode).
2. **Behaviour-cloning initialisation from the heuristic.** **[Inferred]** The bridge result: imitation from a hand-coded human-compatible bot, then search and policy iteration, reached state of the art partnering a pre-existing bot and partnering a human.
3. **Temperature at deployment** (`τ ≈ 1.0` rather than argmax).
4. **Other-play suit symmetry (optional).** Permute the suit axis of `static_actor`, the `card` and `trump` fields of every `PublicEvent`, and the card block of the action space, consistently per episode.

**Limitation:** none of these is validated on Tarneeb; all are transferred from Hanabi and Bridge. A ~30-deal human evaluation is underpowered; report it as qualitative.
